purpose: Pedagogical evaluation of student-teacher explanations. Scores reflect teaching quality in a simulated tutoring conversation, not academic depth.

point_scale.0: Missing or absent — the teacher did not demonstrate this behaviour.
point_scale.1: Partial — attempted but unclear, incomplete, or inconsistent.
point_scale.2: Clear and effective — demonstrated well throughout the conversation.

performance_levels.name: Limited Understanding
performance_levels.interpretation: Explanation was unclear, lacked examples, and showed little responsiveness to the student's confusion.

performance_levels.name: Developing Understanding
performance_levels.interpretation: Core idea was present but explanation lacked structure, examples, or adaptation to confusion.

performance_levels.name: Strong Understanding
performance_levels.interpretation: Clear, well-structured explanation with examples, misconception handling, and good responsiveness.

components.name: Core Concept Delivery
components.label: Core Concept Delivery
components.description: Did the teacher communicate the main idea of the topic correctly and clearly?
components.evaluation_question: Was the central concept explained accurately and in understandable terms?
observable_indicators: States the main idea in plain, accessible language.

mentor_feedback.if_missing: Can you state the main idea of the topic in one or two simple sentences?
mentor_feedback.if_partial: You touched on the main idea — make it clearer and more direct.

components.name: Use of Examples
components.label: Use of Examples
components.description: Did the teacher use at least one concrete, relatable example or analogy?
components.evaluation_question: Did the teacher illustrate the concept with a real-world example or analogy?
observable_indicators: Provides a concrete scenario or analogy.
The example is age-appropriate and clearly connected to the concept.

mentor_feedback.if_missing: Try adding a real-world example or simple analogy to make the idea concrete.
mentor_feedback.if_partial: Your example is close — connect it explicitly back to the main idea.

components.name: Checking Understanding
components.label: Checking Understanding
components.description: Did the teacher check whether the student understood, by asking questions or inviting feedback?
components.evaluation_question: Did the teacher ask the student whether they understood, or invite them to respond?
observable_indicators: Asks 'Does that make sense?', 'Can you explain that back to me?', or similar.
Waits for or responds to the student's level of understanding.

mentor_feedback.if_missing: After explaining, ask the student: 'Does that make sense?' or 'Can you tell me in your own words?'
mentor_feedback.if_partial: Good — make checking understanding a consistent habit, not just once.

components.name: Misconception Handling
components.label: Misconception Handling
components.description: Did the teacher identify and address a common misconception about the topic?
components.evaluation_question: Did the teacher proactively address or correct a misconception expressed by the student?
observable_indicators: Names or acknowledges a wrong belief the student holds.
Explains clearly why the misconception is incorrect.

mentor_feedback.if_missing: What do students often get wrong about this topic? Address that directly.
mentor_feedback.if_partial: You spotted the misconception — now explain clearly *why* it is wrong.

components.name: Adaptive Teaching
components.label: Adaptive Teaching
components.description: Did the teacher adjust their approach when the student expressed confusion or asked follow-up questions?
components.evaluation_question: Did the teacher change strategy (different example, simpler language) in response to student confusion?
observable_indicators: Rephrases or tries a different approach after confusion.
Responds to the specific question the student asked, not a generic answer.

mentor_feedback.if_missing: When the student was confused, try rephrasing or using a completely different example.
mentor_feedback.if_partial: You adapted partially — be more deliberate about tailoring to what the student said.

components.name: Age-Appropriate Language
components.label: Age-Appropriate Language
components.description: Did the teacher avoid excessive jargon and use language appropriate for the student's age?
components.evaluation_question: Was the vocabulary and sentence complexity suitable for the target age group?
observable_indicators: Uses short sentences and everyday vocabulary.

mentor_feedback.if_missing: Your language is too technical — imagine explaining this to a child with no background.
mentor_feedback.if_partial: You used some jargon — when you introduce a technical term, always define it immediately.

components.name: Encouragement & Patience
components.label: Encouragement & Patience
components.description: Did the teacher show patience, warmth, and encouragement throughout the conversation?
components.evaluation_question: Did the teacher respond to confusion with patience and positive reinforcement?
observable_indicators: Acknowledges the student's effort or confusion positively.
Does not show frustration; keeps a supportive tone.

mentor_feedback.if_missing: Acknowledge the student's effort — a simple 'Good question!' goes a long way.
mentor_feedback.if_partial: Good warmth at times — try to keep it consistent throughout.

llm_instructions: You are evaluating the FULL teaching conversation, not a single message.
Assign each component a score of exactly 0, 1, or 2.
Score 0: the behaviour was absent across the entire conversation.
Score 1: the behaviour appeared but was incomplete, inconsistent, or unclear.
Score 2: the behaviour was clearly and effectively demonstrated.
Do NOT default to 0. If there is any evidence of the behaviour, score at least 1.
The 'notes' field must contain a short, specific rationale referencing what the teacher actually said.
Return valid JSON only — no markdown, no extra keys.
